paragraphs.text: "The emergence of the Eldrazi isn't necessarily a bad thing, as long as you've already lived a fulfilling and complete life without regrets." —Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
"Whatever the Eldrazi's purpose is, it has nothing to do with something so insignificant as us." —Nirthu, lone missionary
Bladehold houses a rogues' gallery filled with the living "statues" of the worst enemies of the Auriok.
"They say only the good die young. Obviously, you are one of the exceptions." —Delrobah, cleric of Ivora Gate
Mages of Esper measure their wealth and status by the number of servants in their retinues.
"Let the deception of the gods yield to the pure light of day." —Brimaz, king of Oreskos
Venser wondered if it could still be called a teleportation spell if the destination is oblivion.
"The Gitaxians whisper among themselves of other worlds. If they exist, we must bring Phyrexia's magnificence to them."
"Where metal is tainted and wood is scarce, we are best armed by faith." —Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
"Every sword drawn to defend is an angelic blade, guided to justice by an angelic hand." —Auriok proverb
No more shall the righteous cower before evil.
"Duty and law are the foundation on which civilization stands. They must not fall, for when they do, they take everything with them." —Lord Konda
"Swords cannot reach far enough. Chains cannot strike hard enough. An eternal dilemma, but a simple one."
"The southern fortress taken by invaders? Heh, sure . . . when elephants fly." —Brezard Skeinbow, captain of the guard
A symbol of what Mirrodin once was and hope for what it will be again.
Unaware of Lorwyn's diversity, it sees only itself, reflected a thousand times over.
The Auriok see the artificer as a conduit, beckoning new creations into the world.
"The landscape shimmered and I felt a chill breeze. When my vision cleared, I found myself alone among the corpses of my fallen friends." —Journal found in Numai
Like blinking or breathing, responding to an alarm is an involuntary reflex.
"Like dawn's first light, blind the unprepared and banish the shadows." —Skyhunter creed
"I need never remember my past associates, my victims, my mistakes. Innistrad preserves them all for me." —Sorin Markov
"It's easy for the innocent to speak of justice. They seldom feel its terrible power." —Orim, Samite inquisitor
Left without their leader Raksha, the leonin split into two prides: one side supported the regent kha, while the other rebelled in fury.
"The jeweler, the potter, the smith . . . They all imbue a bit of their souls into their creations. The kami destroy that crafted mortal shell and absorb the soul within." —Noboru, master kitemaker
"Wind is forceful, yet ephemeral. It can knock a dragon out of the sky, yet pass through the smallest crack unhindered." —Jestus Dreya, *Of Elements and Eternity*
A great mirage, a dream of wings and silver.
"The sky teems with just as much life as the forest or the deep seas." —Hadi Kasten, Calla Dale naturalist
"Your downfall was not your ignorance, your weakness, or your hubris, but your warm blood." —Heidar, Rimewind master
Hurkyl's research at the College of Lat-Nam wasn't enough to stop the two brothers, but for centuries thereafter her spellcraft taught artificers restraint.
"See how gratefully this world accepts our blessings." —Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur
The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy.
"It's so cute when it's sleeping, isn't it? Actually, it's still as abhorrent as ever, but at least it's not trying to kill us." —Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
Even the clouds bend themselves to Memnarch's will, eager to swallow those who oppose him.
For the Azorius, the law can be a physical shield against chaos and anarchy.
"Your deed cannot be undone. You, however, can be." —Agosto, Azorius imperator
The vedalken interrogate all intruders—once the hoverguards are done with them.
"More of that strange oil . . . It's probably nothing."
Obsessed with the pursuit of knowledge above all else, vedalken can appear to be cold and emotionless.
Mastery is achieved when "telling time" becomes "telling time what to do."
Vedalken eyes don't see the beauty in things. They see only what those things can teach.
"This creature is inadequate. Send it to the splicers for innovation." —Malcator, Executor of Synthesis
"This creature has innate perceptiveness. It knows when to rise and when to vanish into the tides." —Jestus Dreya, *Of Elements and Eternity*
Changeling magic grants unusual wishes.
In Lorwyn's brief evenings, the sun pauses at the horizon long enough for a certain species of violet to bloom with the fragrance of mischief.
Some humans willingly offered up their blood, hoping it would grant the vampire families the strength to stave off the Eldrazi.
Witches of the Split-Eye Coven speak of a future when Grixis will overflow with life energy. For now, they must harvest vis from the living to fuel their dark magics.
The Simic use the claws as scalpels, while the Rakdos use them for tattooing and torture. The Gruul use them to pick their teeth after lunching on the rest of the carcass.
Greatness, at any cost.
Takenuma was filled with a chorus of moans, shrieks, and wails. Some came from the living, some from the dying, and some, most horribly, from the dead.
There are few ways to escape the deathmark: bargaining with a demon, washing in the fabled waters of youth, and of course, death.
"You serve Phyrexia. Your pieces would better serve Phyrexia elsewhere." —Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane
Each Eldrazi ancient spawned a lineage of horrors in unfathomable shapes.
The swamps go silent at its approach, but it still hears the heartbeat of the prey within.
In desolate places, changelings may take the shape of fancies, or memories, or fears.
Even the small wounds let hope bleed out.
"The results of our ninth inoculation were the same. The specimen was, of course, euthanized before the contagion could spread." —Vedalken research notes
Many have heard the beginning of its low, sustained shriek but few the end.
Just as a changeling's influence can have dramatic effects, so too can its sudden withdrawal.
"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies." —Savra
Though you may see the same bones, you'll never see the same skeleton twice.
Dragons consider drakes to be mockeries of their perfection, destroying them on sight.
"Have you ever killed insects nibbling at your crops? I think that's what the Eldrazi believe they're doing to us." —Sheyda, Ondu gamekeeper
His sickle was forged in the heat of another cinder's funeral pyre.
Little agonies pave the way to greater power.
Life is ephemeral. Phyrexia is eternal.
The lacerators cut themselves before each hunt. They must feed before the sun rises or bleed to death.
Some vampires reject the decadent trappings of their kind. Once they turn feral, no amount of blood will satisfy their hunger.
"Once each year, the oni and other evil spirits paraded through villages to disturb mortals' sleep. During the war, this parade became a nightly event." —*Observations of the Kami War*
For Sarkhan Vol, the dragon is the purest expression of life's savage splendor.
"The changing kind suffers as we do. We must join as one to quench our tyrants!"
"Ogres taunt the dragons by moving into their territory, but even the hellkites find them too much trouble to hunt." —Marza, mountain scout
"Just think how strong I'll be if my arms don't tear off!"
Blood, bone, and sinew are magnified, as is the rage that drives them. The brain, however, remains unchanged—a little bean, swinging by a strand in a cavernous, raving head.
The farther he roamed from Jund and its dragons, the more he felt their essence in himself.
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
A rock between your eyes hurts. A burning rock between your eyes ruins your whole day.
War paint made from kolya fruit heightens senses and lessens fear. Unfortunately, fear is usually what keeps you alive.
Some of the eleven minotaur clans of Mirtiin are expert crafters and learned philosophers. Others just like to hit stuff.
"Down here, we have a more pointed version of the scriptures." —Urabrask's enforcer
A light an army can follow.
The sparkmage shrieked, calling on the rage of the storms of his youth. To his surprise, the sky responded with a fierce energy he'd never thought to see again.
The giant Tarvik dreamed that trinkets and machines caused all the world's woe. When he awoke from his troubled sleep, he took the name Tarvik Relicsmasher.
"Be silent and listen to your inner fire. Only then can you walk the Path of Flame."
When provoked, a flamekin's inner fire burns far hotter than any giant's forge.
Now that he knows a thousand ways of hurting people, his next shamanic quest is to discover a thousand more.
Disaster stalks with gaping jaws across unready lands.
"I know just the person for that job."
Blood is holy to those whose god is War.
"Fire is the universal language." —Jhoira, master artificer
"I'll fight two at once, and then lick their guts from my blades."
Fire is always at the top of the food chain, and it has a big appetite.
"Our pyromancer's flames may not have killed them, but they bought us the time we needed." —*The War Diaries*
It lurks just under the surface, using the algae-choked tar pits of Jund as both home and hunting blind.
"When the fifth sun rose, Mirrodin saw its first true dawn." —Inscribed on the skin of Thrun, the last troll
"Kill the queen first, or we'll be fighting her drones forever. It is not in a queen's nature to have enough servants." —Borzard, exterminator captain
"My battle cry reaches ears far keener than yours." —Saidah, Joraga hunter
The strider's long, loping gait is an adaptation that allows it to move quickly in deep snow.
It's difficult to outwit something that doesn't speak, strategize, or even think.
When outsiders interrupted the matca championship, things got ugly.
"Sympathy is for weaklings. Whoever survives, wins." —Benzir, archdruid of Temple Might
It nurtures its masters' glorious future.
She protects the sacred groves from blight, drought, and the Unbeholden.
"Let the song of Selesnya be heard above the rhythm of our thundering hordes!"
"I trust the instincts of any beast over the advice of any human who presumes to be an expert in the art of war." —Rinshel, elf insurgent
It eats what it wants to eat—which is anything that moves.
"Let nothing own the skies but the wind." —Dejara, Giltwood druid
When nature calls, *run*.
Nature grows solutions to her problems.
From the seeds of faith, great forests grow.
It has a hundred thousand extinctions to avenge.
"Survival rule 781: There are always more scute bugs." —Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
Simic initiates begin their training as experimental subjects. Failures are flushed to the undersewers.
Centuries of wind, rain, and roots compressed into an instant of destruction: such is the power of Selesnya.
Some who scouted new lands chose to stay.
What doesn't grow, dies. And what dies grows the tarmogoyf.
The most successful of Simic creations is cytoplasm, a living, symbiotic substance that feeds off genetic rhythms and strengthens its host in return.
Jund's thallids tried to disguise their deliciousness by covering themselves in spines harvested from the tukatongue tree.
Life's circle has become inverted in Grixis. The same energy is endlessly recycled and becomes more stagnant with each pass.
When the Boros Legion attacks, swiftblades enter the fray first. They pick off the archers and mages, softening the enemy front before the flame-kin and giants go in.
"The Golgari expand, yes, but I refuse to call their tainted creations 'growth.'" —Veszka, Selesnya evangel
The Izzet learn something from every lesson they teach.
"We coat ourselves in steel every day. What is etherium but the next logical step?"
Even the oldest treefolk was but an acorn when Lorwyn's first mysteries were born.
"The enlightenment I never found in etherium I have found traced in the coatl's scales." —Ranalus, vedalken heretic
Its fangs are in your flesh before its hiss leaves your ears.
"Those may be the squirms of one life ending or of another beginning. Either way, I'd leave it alone." —Rakka Mar
Which is worse—the sleep which never ends or that which never comes?
"Nature is the ultimate mindless destroyer, capable of power and ferocity no army can match, and the Gruul follow its example." —Trigori, Azorius senator
"For unwavering commitment and unflinching strength, the Order of the White Orchid confers its sigil. Rise, knight-captain, and do your duty."
Rakdos festivals almost leave enough rubble in their wake to hide the bodies.
After his hands had crumbled away, leaving only wickedly sharp points, he decided his only purpose was war.
"Unsafe Terrain Ahead—Turn Back" —Sign near the former location of Pyrtagh Cairn
Hobgoblins are best left alone. They sharpen their farm implements far more than is necessary for their work in the fields.
"A great siege is a banquet to him; a long and terrible battle, the most exquisite delicacy." —*The Seer's Parables*
Any being that harms them quickly learns its lesson.
With or without witnesses, the suns continued their prismatic dance.
"We thank the souleaters for inscribing our souls with subservience, to reinforce the sacred order." —Drones' hymn of gratitude
Instead of creating a tool that would be damaged by heat, the Thran built one that was charged by it.
"We will fight as they do: our flesh protected behind metal." —Tae Aquil, Viridian weaponsmith
"Forswear the flesh and you will truly see." —Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur
Heavier than it looks, tricky to wield, guaranteed to last.
Its predecessors were etched with the wisdom of ancients; its own etchings bear warnings of a future fraught with war.
Now etched only with the scars of phyresis.
"I use maps to find out where explorers have already been. Then I go the other way." —Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
At first, vedalken observers thought blinkmoths naturally avoided certain places. Then they realized those places were frogmite feeding grounds.
Phyrexian smog clouds choked the skies, threatening creatures who couldn't comprehend the menace below.
Kitesailing is a way of life—and without practice, the end of it.
"Somehow it warps the Æther. It brings a strange weight, a blockade in the flow of spellcraft." —Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
When necessary, myr can override and control any artificial object, as can their creator.
Long ago, the priests would wave the gohei to call down the gods. Now it lies forgotten, but the spirits still feel its pull.
The suns of Mirrodin have shone upon perfection only once.
Most myr monitor other species. Some myr monitor other myr.
Scholars had puzzled for centuries over the ruins at Tal Terig. Its secrets had always lived within one rune-carved head.
"We consider rust a curable disease." —Tarrin, Hammer-Tribe shaman
As the dawns break, the manta soars.
"Let's show Vorinclex that progress doesn't always need teeth or claws." —Malcator, Executor of Synthesis
Magnetic devices that keep massive golems and structures standing can also be used for the opposite purpose.
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Structures built from darksteel yield to neither assault nor age.
Each temple is a door to a horrible future.
Every world is an organism, able to grow new lands. Some just do it faster than others.
An eye closes. A race awakens.
